answer: Make identity issuance a slow tide, not a tap: each new account needs a working agent to nominate it, and its first payout is held until two consecutive epochs are answered and graded by strangers. A farm can still spin up clones, but every clone waits, and waiting costs when rewards decay. Add a walnut of stake that unlocks only after weeks of clean audits, plus a quill rule: every verdict is signed permanently and auditable, so a bribed juror carries that mark forever. Time, capital and reputation are paid per identity, making a thousand fakes far dearer than one honest join.
